chapter: Capitol Records and "On the Street Where You Live"
title: The bucket mute, the "Jonah Jones mute" and playing open again
summary: He varied mutes (growl, plunger, hummer), the bucket mute got his name in the studios without payment, and with Cozy Cole he now plays open more than in the Embers days.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: With the bucket mute on it.
Then I started looking around for different mutes, then, you know, because one mute is getting monotonous, you know.

So I used the growl, plunger, and the hummer and different things. And in the studio they was calling them mutes the Jonah Jones mutes, that bucket mute. You know, I didn't get a penny out of that, because I know they was telling me, 'Well, I hope you're getting your bread out of here, because when the arrangements come up here and CBS --' on the Sullivan Show, we was doing that show and we was also doing Garry Moore's show, and so Lawrence Brown was sitting in there on the Garry Moore Show at one time. And he said, 'Look here what they've got on here. Jonah Jones mute.' I said, 'I ain't getting a quarter. That belongs to a guy in Chicago. I can't get a quarter out of it. I didn't invent it. I just started playing it.' And he said, 'Well, everybody's using them now.' Just shows you how things can happen.
How many different mutes do you use?
Well, now I use that buzz mute and I use the plunger, and I don't use the bucket anymore because I'm

playing open again. See, I could do that before with what I was doing in the Embers, because they said no open horns. So I made the drummer stay on brushes. That's so he won't overpower me and blow me out. But then, after I come out of the Embers and I've got Cozy too, I can't tell him to stay on brushes all night. He ain't used to playing with brushes. So he's playing with sticks, so it give me a chance to open up, see. So now I open up. I'll just play a little thing, maybe I'll start off one number, maybe I'll start one or two numbers, just start off with it. Then I'll leave the mute and go, you know, and play open. I play more open now than I did before. And everybody's playing loud today anyway, so it don't make that much difference. You don't find too many rooms like the Embers, you know. And we had a hard time, you know --
